column1: # LIVENESS DIFFERENTIAL CORPUS — CLOSED INVENTORY.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. Five times running, a check meant to establish that GI-11's replacement
# is genuine degenerated into a check that something by a given name did not fail:
#   round 5  a NAME exists                  -> an empty function satisfied it
#   round 6  a TEST exists                  -> same
#   round 8  a test PASSES                  -> an empty `#[test]` satisfied it
#   round 9  a TARGET exits 0               -> `@true` satisfied it
#   round 9  the SOURCE has the right shape -> renaming the probes to `cg_*` wrappers
#                                              satisfied it, measured
# That is a boundary, not five near misses:
#     NO CHECK THAT LIVES INSIDE THE ARTIFACT CAN ESTABLISH THAT A FUTURE REPLACEMENT OF
#     THAT ARTIFACT IS GENUINE, BECAUSE WHOEVER WRITES THE REPLACEMENT ALSO WRITES THE
#     CHECK.
# What escapes it is a check that can only be satisfied by PRODUCING DIFFERENT ANSWERS ON
# INPUTS WHOSE CORRECT ANSWERS ARE ALREADY FIXED. This file is those inputs. A renamed
# wrapper around the lexical probe cannot pass it, because what is checked is the model's
# VERDICTS on these programs, not its spelling. The same move as replacing a re-implemented
# module parser with `cargo test --list`.
# THE ANSWERS ARE FIXED BY REVIEW, NOT BY THE MODEL. Each `answer` below is the ground
# truth about the program, decided by reading it. Changing an answer to make a model pass
# is a change to what liveness MEANS, and it is a diff a reviewer can see. That is the
# whole protection, and it is the same one tests/conformance-manifest.txt relies on.
# THE CORPUS IS RED TODAY, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Every other precondition this gate has
# tried could be satisfied by an artifact that did nothing. This one is failed by the
# model that is actually wired, on cases that model actually gets wrong. `make thesis-exit`
# refuses until it passes.
# COLUMNS (TAB-separated, all six mandatory):
#   id  answer  subject  source  why  source-of-truth
# answer:   live | dead     the GROUND TRUTH about `subject` in `source`.
# subject:  the function whose liveness is being asked about.
# source:   a whole compilation unit, `\n` for newline. Kept inline rather than as .pd
#           files because tests/conformance-manifest.txt is a closed inventory over every
#           .pd under tests/, and these are not conformance fixtures.
# why:      the reasoning a reviewer checks the answer against.
# source-of-truth: `reviewed` (decided by reading) or a file:line this shape was measured at.
# WHAT THESE CASES DO NOT ESTABLISH. Reviewers put the ceiling plainly: a lexical
# classifier could score full marks by recognising the three literal divergence forms and
# then following at most one named intermediary from `main`. The metamorphic variants below
# raise the cost of ONE part of that, and the claim is narrowed to what they do: alpha-
# renaming, reordering and inert whitespace defeat an EXACT SOURCE FINGERPRINT. They do NOT
# defeat the classifier described above — `if true { return; }`, `while true` and
# `if false` all survive those transformations intact, and the deepest positive still has a
# single intermediary. Defeating that would need a divergence restructured into a
# semantically identical but lexically different form, which is not in this corpus.
# NO FINITE CORPUS REMOVES THE HUMAN-REVIEW BOUNDARY. This corpus proves the model's
# VERDICTS on cases a reviewer fixed. It says nothing about the model's STRUCTURE: scoped
# call-site identities, declared entry roots, an order-independent fixed point, provenance,
# per-edge completion, indirect targets resolved-or-declared. That is GI-11's observable,
# and GI-11 requires BOTH — this corpus and tests/callgraph-differential.tsv — precisely
# because neither substitutes for the other. A named test was tried for the structural half
# and removed in round 12: an empty test body reported success and satisfied it whole. Feasibility that needs interprocedural constant propagation is
# deliberately out of scope here and belongs to the observable.
# A model must answer every row. REFUSING IS FAILING: a model that cannot decide these is
# not the replacement GI-11 requires. R4's honest refusal is the right behaviour for the
# LEXICAL model and is exactly why the lexical model does not satisfy GI-11.
# id
column4: source
column5: why

column1: # --- DEAD: the three shapes that broke every lexical design ---------------------------
diverging-if
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { if true { return; } ornament(); }
column5: the `if` always diverges, so nothing after it runs

column1: while-true
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { while true { } ornament(); }
column5: the loop never completes

column1: false-branch
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { if false { ornament(); } }
column5: the guard is constant-false

column1: unreferenced
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { }
column5: nothing names it at all

column1: dead-caller
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn dead() -> i64 { return ornament(); }\nfn main() { }
column5: its only caller is itself unreachable

column1: self-recursive
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return ornament(); }\nfn main() { }
column5: a self-edge is not a path from main

column1: # --- LIVE: the converse, so "answer dead everywhere" fails too -------------------------
direct
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { ornament(); }
column5: called at the top level of main

column1: via-callee
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn mid() -> i64 { return ornament(); }\nfn main() { mid(); }
column5: reached through one hop

column1: inside-else
column4: fn compile_file(p: String) { print(p); }\nfn main() { let n: i64 = arg_count(); if n < 3 { print("usage"); } else { compile_file("x"); } }
column5: a conditional branch is REACHABLE; a naive under-approximation calls this dead, and it is the real witness's own shape

column1: loop-body
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { let i: i64 = 0; while i < 3 { ornament(); i = i + 1; } }
column5: a loop body that may execute is reachable

column1: after-conditional
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn side() { print("x"); }\nfn main() { if true { side(); } ornament(); }
column5: the `if` completes, so what follows runs

column1: in-initializer
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { let v: i64 = ornament(); print_int(v); }
column5: a call in a `let` INITIALIZER evaluates. (Named `in-return-expr` until round 11; it was never a return expression, and GI-11's contract names initializers, conditions and return expressions as three separate shapes)

column1: in-condition
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { if ornament() > 0 { print("y"); } }
column5: a call in a CONDITION evaluates before either branch is chosen

column1: in-return-expr
column4: fn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn mid() -> i64 { return ornament(); }\nfn main() { print_int(mid()); }
column5: a call in a RETURN EXPRESSION evaluates; truncating at the `return` token loses it

column1: # The same programs under transformations that CANNOT change liveness: alpha-renaming,
# reordering definitions, and inert whitespace. What they establish, exactly: a model that
# answers by EXACT SOURCE FINGERPRINT scores differently on a variant than on its base, and
# a correct model cannot tell them apart. What they do NOT establish: they do not defeat a
# classifier that recognises `if true { return; }`, `while true` or `if false`, because
# every variant preserves those forms verbatim. scripts/thesis_exit.py pins each variant to
# its base in VARIANT_OF_BASE and requires the two to be scored identically.
mm-diverging-if-renamed
column4: fn decoration() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { if true { return; } decoration(); }
column5: alpha-renamed `diverging-if`; the answer cannot depend on the identifier

column1: mm-while-true-reordered
column4: fn main() { while true { } ornament(); }\nfn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }
column5: `while-true` with the definition AFTER main; order is not semantics

column1: mm-direct-spaced
column5: `direct` with inert whitespace and newlines

column1: mm-via-callee-renamed
column4: fn deep() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn hop() -> i64 { return deep(); }\nfn main() { hop(); }
column5: alpha-renamed `via-callee`

column1: mm-false-branch-reordered
column4: fn main() { if false { ornament(); } }\nfn ornament() -> i64 { return 1; }
column5: `false-branch` with the definition after main

column1: mm-inside-else-renamed
column4: fn build(p: String) { print(p); }\nfn main() { let n: i64 = arg_count(); if n < 3 { print("usage"); } else { build("x"); } }
column5: alpha-renamed `inside-else`, the real witness's shape
